In the rest–frame of the glass the light travels with the usual reduced speed  

 u′ = c/n = 1/n .  

The glass itself moves with speed v in the same direction as the beam toward the laboratory observer.  
To obtain the speed u of the light with respect to the laboratory we use the relativistic velocity–addition formula for collinear velocities (c = 1):

 u = (u′ + v)/(1 + u′ v)
   = (1/n + v)/(1 + v/n)
   = (1 + n v)/(n + v).

(A) 1  
(B) (1+n v)/(n−v)  
(C) (1−n v)/(n+v)  
(D) (1+n v)/(n+v)

The result matches option (D).

Answer: D
